analysis:
This PR changes documentation only; no source code was supplied. Changes: docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md head lines 802-810 and docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md head lines 125, 269, 377 and 381. They describe per-file lease coordination for complete-checkpoint reads (SSDCheckpointFileCoordinator.swift), mtime refresh throttled to ttlSeconds/30, and how TTL and budget retirement treat busy files.

Threat T-041 (bound (b), SEC-035) requires the 30-minute sliding TTL to bound reuse. The described behavior does not extend retention past 30 minutes from the last hit:
- The mtime can trail the last hit by up to 60 s, or stay unrefreshed under overlapping hits. That makes restart scans expire files earlier, which is conservative.
- Whole-root TTL expiry keeps a file only if its in-memory last hit is within the TTL, then records that hit as the mtime.
- Future mtimes are rewritten, which limits mtime-based freshness inflation.
- defaultTTLSeconds and maxTTLSeconds stay 1800, so no new SEC-035 sign-off is triggered.
- Budget eviction ordered by a stale mtime may evict recently hit files early. That affects availability and wear only, not confidentiality.
- A busy corrupt file stays indexed and fails later reads until removed or expired. This is a bounded local cold-path fallback. AES-GCM authentication still rejects it, so integrity is unchanged.
- No HMAC name derivation, AAD, KEK or salt-scope text changed.

Remaining integration questions, unverifiable here because no source was supplied:
- The SSDCheckpointFileCoordinator, SSDOwnedEntryRetirement and SSDWholeRootMaintainer implementations must actually enforce the documented rules: the exclusive lease for retirement, the unusedSince = now - ttlSeconds check, and never setting an mtime newer than the real last hit.
- Ancestor files in a delta chain are read unlocked (reference line 267/268). Integration should confirm that TTL retirement cannot keep ancestors alive beyond the TTL through leaf hits beyond what was already documented.

No regression was identified from the documentation evidence.
